questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?

block.label: Quick Recall
block.sub: Four options, one answer — keep it fast

questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². Always halve after multiplying base by height.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: What two areas does a cylinder's total surface area combine?

block.label: Scrub It
block.sub: Rub out the wrong answers with your finger

questions.answer: Curved area and two circle ends
questions.why: A cylinder's total surface area is the curved surface plus the area of both circular ends — missing the second circle is a common error.
options: Curved area and two circle ends
Curved area and one circle end

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 16 cm and a height of 11 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 16 × 11 = 88 cm². Say the formula before multiplying to avoid rushing past the halving step.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: From a while back — in Lord of the Flies, what does Jack mainly represent?
questions.why: Jack symbolises savagery, violence, and the desire for power, contrasting with Ralph's focus on order and rescue.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In a sealed container, 15g of reactants react completely. What is the mass of the products?
questions.why: Mass is conserved in a closed system, so the products have the same total mass as the reactants: 15g.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What do we call a solid that suddenly forms when two liquids react?
questions.why: A precipitate is a solid that forms from a reaction between two liquids, showing a chemical change has happened.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: A snack ad shows teenagers laughing at a party eating chips. What technique is this?
questions.why: This technique links a product to a fun, desirable lifestyle so viewers associate the snack with good feelings, not its actual health value.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: On a nutrition label, which nutrient group does sugar get listed under?
questions.answer: Carbohydrates, since sugar is one type
questions.why: Sugar is a simple carbohydrate, so nutrition labels list it as a sub-type under the carbohydrate total, not under protein, fat, or fibre.
options: Carbohydrates, since sugar is one type
